TOP OF BOOK

  • BRENT / HORMUZ TALKS (MACRO) [DELTA ▲] — Brent pulling back from recent spike toward ~$79/barrel as US-Iran/Oman interim deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz appears imminent; Houthi Red Sea attack briefly reversed the move.
    • Vs. baseline: Brent had spiked sharply on renewed US-Iran exchanges of strikes after the June ceasefire unravelled in July, hitting above $100 in late July before retreating. As of 5 Aug, Brent was fluctuating below $76/barrel on optimism that a 60-day interim agreement to reopen the Strait — with no tolls — was close, with Washington aiming to announce as early as Aug 5. The Houthi attack (Red Sea, 5 Aug) re-introduced intraday volatility; no deal signed yet as of this morning.
    • Read: Oil pricing in roughly 10% weekly decline as the most liquid contracts accumulate ~10% losses on the week. The Hormuz path is the critical variable: even if the war ends, global energy flows are expected to take months to fully recover, with 500+ vessels estimated to be waiting to exit the Gulf and mine-clearing taking weeks minimum. For EU banks — dual-channel. Lower energy prices reduce the ECB's compulsion to hike in September, extending the rate pause and compressing NII tailwind assumptions. Conversely, any re-escalation snaps oil back and re-prices the September hike as a near-certainty. Markets currently see a 70% chance of a September hike, the oil-price surge having outweighed the relatively dovish tone at the Sintra forum. ECB deposit rate sits at 2.25% post-June hike. A Hormuz deal removing the energy shock premium is the single biggest swing factor for the rate path — and thus for European bank NII hedging positions. Credit spread: calmer oil = risk-on for bank HY/senior spreads, periphery compression. Watch BTP-Bund. For insurers (Allianz, Munich Re), energy price normalisation reduces claims inflation pressure on P&C lines.
    • Next step: DIG IN — monitor Hormuz deal confirmation or collapse. Any confirmed signing = immediate re-pricing of September ECB hike probability lower; sell EUR rates vol. Houthi escalation = reverse. This is the top cross-asset trade today.
    • Sources: Trading Economics crude data, The National, Ground.News / Transport Topics
  • ECB RATE PATH (MACRO) [DELTA ▼] — September +25bp partially repriced lower as oil retreats; market not yet abandoning the hike.
    • Vs. baseline: The ECB held rates at 2.25% in July. Lagarde stated that renewed Middle East hostilities pose upside risk to inflation; traders were already pricing a September hike. All respondents in a Bloomberg survey predicted no change in July; most then anticipated a +25bp increase in September, taking the deposit rate to 2.50%. The Hormuz de-escalation today creates a dovish contingency — if oil settles durably below $80, the ECB may pause again in September.
    • Read: For European bank positioning, the September decision is the NII swing event. A hike at 2.50% extends the deposit-rate support for liability margins — ING specifically guided commercial NII of €16.8–17bn for 2026, with liability margin expected above 110bps in 2027–28. A pause instead opens the NII-compression trade. Watch EUR OIS curve for September repricing as today's Hormuz newsflow develops. Equities: rate pause = modest NII headwind but positive for credit quality; AT1s broadly positive on lower vol.
    • Next step: MONITOR — oil/Hormuz resolution is the gate. No independent ECB action this week. Next meeting Sep 10.
    • Sources: CNBC/ECB July press conference, Bloomberg survey, Trading Economics ECB

BY NAME / THEME

  • ING GROUP (INGA) [DELTA ▲] — Q2 2026 beat with upgraded full-year and 2027 guidance; fee income target pulled forward by one year. Already reported (~30 July), but guidance upgrades are still the live positioning anchor.
    • Vs. baseline: Q2 net result reached €1,947m, up 16% YoY; H1 net result up 14% to €3,492m, driven by strong NII and fee income and supported by accelerated customer growth (1.1mn new mobile primary customers YoY). Full-year commercial NII outlook raised to €16.8–17bn; ING now expects to reach €5bn in fee income in 2026, one year earlier than initially planned. Q2 ROTE hit 17%; CET1 improved to 13.1%.
    • Read: Guidance upgrade on fee income acceleration is the non-consensus angle — this is structural diversification, not rate sensitivity. Reduces the bear case that ING is leveraged only to the rate cycle. Equity: positive; AT1 spreads should be stable to tighter. The 50% capital allocation to regular dividends plus ~40% to buybacks/additional distributions is a meaningful return story. Risk: a September ECB pause on Hormuz de-escalation would marginally dent NII uplift but not reverse the guidance upgrade.
    • Next step: MONITOR — no near-term catalyst; update NII model for Hormuz/ECB scenario.
    • Sources: TradingView / MarketBeat, Investing.com
  • DEUTSCHE BANK (DBK) [IN LINE] — Record H1 post-tax profit of €4.1bn; Q2 revenue +9% YoY; shares fell slightly on EPS miss vs consensus.
    • Vs. baseline: Q2 net revenues of €8.5bn; H1 net revenues of €17.2bn; post-tax profit for H1 at €4.1bn — highest half-year result in the bank's history. Cost-income ratio 60.9%; ROE 12%+ across all divisions; CET1 at 13.9%, in line with 13.5–14.0% operating range. EPS missed consensus by ~30% (revenue beat by ~4%) — the gap is likely DTA/tax-line noise rather than underlying. New €500m buyback announced to follow completion of the current €1bn programme.
    • Read: Binary resolved — record H1 is off the table as a risk. The equity dip on EPS miss is a noise trade; the revenue beat and 20 consecutive quarters of YoY revenue growth are the durable signal. CET1 at 13.9% (top of operating range) supports continued buyback execution. Stock weakness = add opportunity for long-term holders. Equity leg: constructive. Credit/AT1: stable, no capital stress. NII outlook for H2 remains gated on the September ECB decision; a hike to 2.50% would extend deposit-rate support for DB's liability margins.
    • Next step: NO ACTION — wait for Hormuz/ECB to clarify NII path for H2.
    • Sources: Deutsche Bank IR, Investing.com transcript
  • GREEK BANKS — Alpha / Eurobank / Piraeus / NBG [DELTA ▲] — Post-Q2 Morgan Stanley target upgrades this morning; Piraeus dividend (€0.40/share) pays today (7 Aug).
    • Vs. baseline: Morgan Stanley raised Alpha Bank target to €5.00 (from €4.90) and NBG to €17.60 (from €17.20); maintained Eurobank as preferred long-term story despite 2026 EPS trim on Eurolife transaction delays, citing stronger 2027 NII and lower cost of risk. Eurobank was the only Greek bank to substantially upgrade its 2026 lending growth target; also the only lender to reduce NPE ratio and improve coverage simultaneously. Piraeus paying €0.40/share cash dividend on 7 August.
    • Read: Morgan Stanley expects NII and fees to drive stronger profitability at Piraeus; says Greek banks offer "one of the most attractive combinations of growth and valuation in Europe," with particular preference for Piraeus and Eurobank. The Eurolife delay is a 2026-specific drag on Eurobank — watch for a Q3 close, which would be a positive re-rating event. The Piraeus dividend today removes the ex-date risk. Equity leg: remain long Eurobank and Piraeus. Credit: Greek sovereign spread relative to Bunds is a tail risk if the ECB hikes further and the energy shock depresses Greek tourism, weighing on domestic NII growth assumptions.
    • Next step: MONITOR — watch Eurolife transaction close date; any acceleration = positive catalyst for Eurobank.
    • Sources: Cyprus Mail (Morgan Stanley report), Piraeus H1 2026 IR presentation
  • ADYEN (ADYEN) [NEW] — CFO Ethan Tandowsky departure effective August 2026; successor search initiated. H1 2026 results on 13 August.
    • Vs. baseline: CFO Ethan Tandowsky announced his departure effective August 2026; search for successor initiated. This is a management change landing immediately ahead of the H1 print. H1 2026 Shareholder Letter publishes 13 August; earnings call at 3pm CEST same day. Q1 2026 was solid — Adyen reaffirmed 20–22% constant-currency net revenue growth for 2026; management flagged Q2 should improve as APAC comps ease, with H1/H2 growth broadly similar.
    • Read: CFO departure at a company mid-growth cycle and one week before a major print is a yellow flag, not a red one — but the timing is adverse. The prior H2 2025 print showed continued customer-led growth with ~21% constant-currency net revenue growth and ~55% EBITDA margin. Street consensus is €672m revenue for H1. A miss here combined with a CFO vacuum would be a significant negative re-rating. Equity leg: reduce into the print, reassess post-13 Aug; the stock has corrected from €1,600 to ~€940, already discounting some growth deceleration. Credit: A- rated, senior notes not in stress; funding costs unaffected by the management transition at current spreads.
    • Next step: DIG IN — confirm CFO transition timeline and any interim arrangements before the 13 Aug call. Size of position should be trimmed until successor announced.
    • Sources: Quartr Adyen IR summary, Adyen IR events

CREDIT CORNER

  • ATHENE / APOLLO (APO) [NEW] — Athene prices $1bn 6.150% senior notes due 2036, closing 7 August; proceeds for general corporate purposes including subsidiary capital contributions.
    • Vs. baseline: Athene agreed to sell $1bn aggregate principal of 6.150% senior notes due 2036; expected close 7 August. Proceeds for general corporate purposes, including capital contributions to insurance subsidiaries to support organic growth. Total assets at Athene of $448bn as of March 31, 2026. Athene also has a Fixed Income Investor call scheduled for 13 August with senior management discussing business trends and new business origination.
    • Read: 6.15% coupon for a 10-year senior from an Apollo/Athene vehicle — this is the all-in funding cost that benchmarks the spread between private-credit return and liability cost. The deal clearing at investment grade reflects market access is intact for the major alt-credit platforms despite the BDC redemption noise. However, the coupon premium vs. comparable IG financials is the watch — any widening here signals funding cost stress for the annuity/insurance-linked private credit model. Leg: IG credit, directional read for Apollo equity. Next step: check clearing spread vs. Athene's existing 2054 curve (last priced at 6.25% in March 2024) — tighter or wider tells you whether market is re-rating the business positively.
    • Next step: MONITOR — watch the 13 Aug investor call for any commentary on deployment pace given BDC gating headwinds.
    • Sources: Investing.com, Manila Times / GlobeNewswire
  • US NON-TRADED BDC SECTOR — BCRED / Blue Owl / HPS / FS KKR [DELTA ▼] — Q2 redemption gating confirmed at record levels; non-accruals rising; BDC fundraising crashed 74% YoY in April. European read-through: real but lagged.
    • Vs. baseline: Industry-wide redemption requests hit $13.9bn in Q1 2026, the first time on record that requests exceeded new fundraising; Q2 requests climbed to $15.6bn against only $5.9bn paid out. BCRED, Blue Owl OBDC II, and HPS Corporate Lending Fund all disclosed similar gating dynamics. Non-accruals jumped from 0.6% to 2.4% at cost between Q1 and Q2; Medallia (customer analytics, $1.1bn cost basis) dropped to 60 cents on the dollar; Affordable Care International fell to 70 cents.
    • Read: The US BDC stress is a structural liquidity mismatch, not a credit meltdown — but rising non-accruals at 2.4% cost is no longer dismissible noise. The European read-through: (1) European direct lenders with US software exposure (Ares, Goldman Sachs Private Credit, Arcmont) should be screened for portfolio overlap; (2) Hayfin's closed-end DLF V (see below) is positioned as the explicit alternative to semi-liquid vehicles — this stress validates that positioning and should attract LP capital to European drawdown funds over US BDCs; (3) bank syndication desks benefit marginally as BDC gating re-directs some large-cap deal flow back to the loan market, easing spread compression and supporting NII on newly originated leveraged loans. Watch for any European BDC/ELTIF vehicles facing similar pressure.
    • Next step: DIG IN — cross-reference Ares, Apollo, Goldman private credit European portfolios for software/tech concentration overlap with Medallia/Affordable Care.
    • Sources: Angel Investors Network, With Intelligence, PitchBook / BofA
  • HAYFIN — Direct Lending Fund V (€15bn close) [NEW] — Largest European private credit fundraise on record; >2x predecessor; 50% already deployed.
    • Vs. baseline: Hayfin closed DLF V at >€15bn, significantly exceeding its target; more than 50% of commitments already deployed across 35+ companies at time of close. Hayfin built minimal exposure to software credits most susceptible to AI disruption; deployed a record €7.1bn in direct lending transactions in the last twelve months. Hayfin explicitly positioned the closed-end structure as a contrast to semi-liquid US vehicles facing redemption pressure.
    • Read: Increased competition between direct lending and the BSL market has compressed European direct lending margins, with participants describing 475bps as the "new 500." €15bn of new dry powder at Hayfin alone is significant supply-side pressure on spreads for European mid-market (€50m–€300m unitranche) — this further compresses returns for existing vintages and tightens the NII-equivalent yield on direct lending relative to bank loan books. The 50% deployment at close is unusual speed and signals aggressive origination pace; watch for loan quality and covenant quality degradation as the fund races to deploy the rest. Read-through to bank syndication: large-cap flow still shared; mid-market banks (Commerzbank SME arm, ING mid-market) may see increased competition for the same credits at tighter terms.
    • Next step: MONITOR — watch Octus/Debtwire for Hayfin deal flow and any covenant-lite drift signals in H2 2026.
    • Sources: Hayfin Capital Management, Private Credit Europe
